Ng, K.W., Giroux, L., MacPhee, T. and Todoschuk, T. (2012). Incorporation of Charcoal in Coking Coal Blend - A Study of the Effects on Carbonization Conditions and Coke Quality. AISTech 2012 Proceedings, Association for Iron & Steel Technology. CanmetENERGY (NRCan) and ArcelorMittal Dofasco.

BACKGROUND ONLY - no main file written. Pilot-scale (350 kg movable-wall oven) carbonization trials with 2-5% charcoal in coal blends: blend chemistry, rheology, petrography, wall pressure and coke cold/hot strength. No plant-level energy, cost, or emissions per t coke; pilot coke yields (74.4-77.7%) are oven-trial values, not plant performance. What it has: Tables I-IV: blend proximate/ultimate/ash chemistry, Gieseler and dilatation, petrography, coke yield, size, ASTM stability and hardness, IRSID, CRI and CSR at 0-5% charcoal (coarse and fine). Finding: fine charcoal keeps cold strength but cuts CSR more; demineralisation and briquetting needed. Canada 2010 context statistics (sector-intensity file). Not the Ng et al. 2012 Iron and Steel Technology article UKERC cites (ng_2012_001); prints none of the UKERC IS-IW12 figures.
